# Nomenclature

The manuscript and code files may utilize different naming conventions for groups and treatments as follows:

**Manuscript Name**  | **Related Script Name(s)**
------------- | -------------
Sample Type  | Type
Microbial Depletion  | Depletion, Dep, or Treatment
Microbial Density  | Concentration, Con, PW_Percentage, or Percentage
Pond Source | Pond, or Pond_Treatment

# Jonckheere Terpstra Test {.tabset}

## Description

To test for a monotonic (a function between ordered sets that preserves the given order) trend (correlation) across ordered groups (i.e., ordinal IV), this code will use a Jonckheere-Terpstra Test. Your dependent variable must be continuous or ordinal, and you must expect increasing or decreasing trends (not just any difference).

The exact calculation requires that there be no ties and that the sample size is less than 100.

When data are tied and sample size is at most 100 permutation p-value is returned. Recommend that the user set nperm to be 1000 or higher if permutation p-value is desired.

```{r seed, include=FALSE}
## SET SEED
set.seed(745869)
### This will allow others to reproduce your exact numbers.
```

## Gut Samples {.tabset .tabset-pills}

### PLE

```{r Gut_PLE, warning=FALSE}
gut <- read.csv("/Taxa_Abundance_Statistics/Gut_Con_RelAbun.csv", header = TRUE)

gutple <- gut[ which(gut$Pond == "PLE"), ]

#### Formula of the form lhs ~ rhs where lhs gives the data values and rhs the corresponding groups.

jt_results_gutple <- gutple %>%
  group_by(Taxonomic_Family) %>%
  summarise(
    JT_statistic = JonckheereTerpstraTest(Rel_Abun ~ Percentage, nperm = 5000)$statistic,
    P_value = JonckheereTerpstraTest(Rel_Abun ~ Percentage, nperm = 5000)$p.value
  ) %>%
  mutate(BH_adj_pval = p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"))

jt_results_gutple
write.csv(jt_results_gutple, "Gut_PLECon_JT_BHadj_pvals2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### PM


# Multiple Comparison Corrections for Kruskal-Wallis {.tabset}

Here we are importing tables of Dunn's p-values (calculated in Prism) because we did these tests across 12 different taxon. Dunn's is already corrected for within-taxon comparisons, but we need to correct for doing this 12 separate times.

## Gut Samples {.tabset .tabset-pills}

### Depletion

```{r GutDep, warning=FALSE}
df <- read.csv("/Taxa_Abundance_Statistics/Gut_Dep_Dunns_ForCorrection.csv", header = TRUE, row.names=1)

long_df <- df %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Comparison") %>%  # move row names to a column if needed
  pivot_longer(cols = -Comparison, 
               names_to = "Taxon", 
               values_to = "Pval")

long_df$BH_adj_pval <- p.adjust(long_df$Pval, method = "BH")
head(long_df)
write.csv(long_df, "Gut_Dep_BHadj_pvals2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Source

